{{nihongo|'''Mefu Shrine'''|売布神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Mefu Yamate-chō, {{ill|Takarazuka, Hyōgo|Q823967|qid=Q823967}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Mefu Shrine'''|売布神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* Main deity – {{ill|Shitateruhime|fr|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|simple|Shitateru-hime|zh|下照姬|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateru-hime-no-Kami}} (Takahi-me-no-Kami)
* Associated deity – {{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|Q10940674|qid=Q10940674|lt=Ame-no-Wakahiko-no-Kami}}

The surrounding area was the base of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}} lineage known as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakayue no Muraji}} (わかゆえのむらじ). It is believed that the original enshrined deity was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ofume no Muraji}} (おおめふのむらじ), the ancestor of the Wakayue no Muraji,<ref>According to the “Takahashi-shi Bun.” In the “Tenson Hongi,” this figure appears as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōmefu no Mikoto}} (おおめふのみこと).</ref>.

== History ==
The shrine is traditionally said to have been founded in the 18th year of {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} ({{ill|610|Q30326|qid=Q30326}}). According to legend, {{ill|Shitateruhime|fr|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|simple|Shitateru-hime|zh|下照姬|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateru-hime-no-Kami}} took pity on the local villagers who were suffering from hunger and cold, taught them how to plant rice, spin hemp, and weave cloth, and after the villagers became prosperous they enshrined Shitateru-hime-no-Kami. The origin of the name Kometani Village is also said to derive from this legend, either as a corruption of “mai-tane” (sown rice seed) or “Mefu Valley” (Mefu-tani).

In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the shrine was listed as a minor shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

From the medieval period onward, it was known as Kibune Shrine or Kibune Myōjin (Kifune Daimyōjin). However, in the first year of {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} ({{ill|1736|Q6989|qid=Q6989}}), a survey conducted by {{ill|Namikawa Seisho|Q6563872|qid=Q6563872}}, who had been ordered by the {{ill|Jisha-bugyō|Q1036279|qid=Q1036279}} {{ill|Ōoka Tadasuke|Q1054143|qid=Q1054143}} to compile regional gazetteers, identified this shrine as the Shikinaisha Mefu Shrine. Thereafter, it came to be known as Mefu Shrine.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6), it was designated as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

== Shrine grounds ==
* Main hall – Rebuilt in {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} 13 ({{ill|1816|Q6953|qid=Q6953}}). A {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=cypress bark roofing}}. It was damaged in the {{ill|Damage by Great Hanshin earthquake|Q11392882|qid=Q11392882}} but later restored.
* Worship hall (Haiden)
* Ichikishima Shrine – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Shrine}}
* Toyotama Shrine – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}
* Remote worship site for the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}
* Shrine office
* Float storage

== Cultural properties ==
== Tangible Cultural Properties designated by Takarazuka City ==
[[File:Mefu-jinja (Takarazuka), sekihi.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shrine name stone marker}}]]
* Mefu Shrine name stone marker (with: two documents) (archaeological materials) – Erected in the first year of {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} ({{ill|1736|Q6989|qid=Q6989}}). The accompanying designation includes the original and a copy of “Memo on the Stone Monument of Mefu Shrine.” Designated on March 30, {{ill|1976|Q2480|qid=Q2480}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 51).<ref name="Takarazuka Cultural Properties">[http://www.city.takarazuka.hyogo.jp/kyoiku/rekishi/1003729.html Cultural Properties of Takarazuka] (Takarazuka City website).</ref>

== Natural Monuments designated by Takarazuka City ==
* Mefu Shrine grove – Designated on March 30, 1976 (Shōwa 51).<ref name="Takarazuka Cultural Properties"/>

== Annual festival ==
The {{ill|Danjiri Matsuri|Q5219928|qid=Q5219928}} held on October 18 and 19 is co-hosted with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasaka Shrine}} ({{ill|Takarazuka, Hyōgo|Q823967|qid=Q823967}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kiyoshikōjin}}), during which two {{ill|danjiri|Q11424706|qid=Q11424706}}—one from Kometani East (Mefu, Kometani) and one from Kometani West (Kiyoshikōjin)—enter the shrine precincts.

== Location and access ==
* 1-1 Mefu Yamate-chō, Takarazuka City, Hyōgo Prefecture
* 5-minute walk from {{ill|Mefu-Jinja Station|Q6807953|qid=Q6807953}} on the {{ill|Hankyu Takarazuka Main Line|Q3832859|qid=Q3832859}}
